critique.good: The tier names stay intact, the two numeric columns are easy to scan, and both longer support descriptions fit within two lines. The rows read clearly as units.
critique.problems: The support column is relatively tight, producing an early break in both longer descriptions. The numeric columns have some room that could be reassigned.

critique.good: The uptime header fits on one line, and the numeric values align clearly.
critique.problems: Mission-critical breaks at its hyphen, weakening the row label. The Professional support description takes three lines, making that row noticeably taller and less even.
critique.cause: The 110px tier column is too narrow for the full name, while the 228px uptime column leaves only 281px for support.

critique.good: The wider support column gives the descriptions a comfortable two-line rhythm, and the numeric columns remain compact and scannable.
critique.problems: Mission-critical breaks at its hyphen, so the most distinctive tier label occupies two lines. The credit header is also closely fitted.

critique.good: Tier names and percentages stay intact, and the two numeric columns are easy to scan. Both longer support descriptions fit in two lines.
critique.problems: The Mission-critical support description leaves “manager” alone on its second line, making that cell look uneven. The credit header also occupies two lines.
critique.cause: The 348px support column fits nearly the entire Mission-critical description on its first line; the 100px credit column is too narrow for its header on one line.

critique.good: The wider numeric columns give their headers slightly more room, while the tier names and values remain clear. Support descriptions still fit in two lines.
critique.problems: The extra numeric-column space does not remove either header wrap, and “manager” remains isolated on the second support line.
critique.cause: Widths of 155px and 105px still do not fit the respective headers on one line. The remaining 333px support column still allows the Mission-critical first line to run too long.

critique.good: The wider support column gives the descriptions more room, while tier names and numeric values remain intact and scannable.
critique.problems: The Mission-critical description still ends with an isolated “manager.” The narrow numeric headers remain wrapped, so the additional support width does not improve the overall rhythm.
critique.cause: The 363px support column still falls short of fitting the description on one line, and the 135px and 95px numeric columns cannot fit their headers on one line.

critique.good: Tier names and percentages remain intact, and the numeric columns are easy to scan. The service credit header stays on one line, while support descriptions wrap at word boundaries.
critique.problems: The last support description leaves “manager” alone on its second line. The uptime column also has more width than it needs for its two-line header and short values.
critique.cause: The 322px support column forces the last word onto a line by itself; the 150px uptime column consumes space that could be given to support.

critique.good: The wider uptime column gives its header and values comfortable space. Tier names and percentages remain intact, and the support descriptions wrap cleanly.
critique.problems: The service credit header wraps, making both numeric headers two lines tall without improving the support column’s line breaks. The final support description still ends with a lone “manager.”
critique.cause: Reducing service credit to 100px forces its header to wrap, while increasing uptime to 170px leaves support at only 323px.

critique.good: This is the strongest of the three: the uptime header remains legible on two lines, service credit stays on one line, and the extra support width gives the descriptive column better proportion. Tier names and percentages remain intact.
critique.problems: The last support description still leaves “manager” alone on its second line, and the professional-tier description remains unevenly distributed across its two lines.
critique.cause: The 337px support column is wider than in the other designs but still does not produce more balanced breaks in these descriptions.

understanding.purpose: Compare SLA tiers by uptime commitment, service credit, and available support.
understanding.reading: Readers scan tier names down the first column, compare commitments and credits across rows, then read support details within each tier. Longer support descriptions will set row heights, giving headers and other cells room to wrap where needed.
groups: Monthly uptime commitment and service credit are comparable numeric terms; their values should be easy to scan down their columns.
Tier identifies each row, while support channels describe the service available for that tier.
keep_intact: Uptime percentages and service credit percentages
may_wrap: Monthly uptime commitment and Service credit headers at word boundaries
Support channel descriptions at word boundaries

bad.why: The narrow uptime column forces its header onto three lines, making the header disproportionately tall without improving the support entries.
The uptime header takes three lines and creates an unnecessarily tall header for a small table.

final.rationale: r2C keeps the tier names intact and gives the long support descriptions most of the available width. The service-credit header stays on one line, while the uptime header wraps naturally into two; both numeric columns remain easy to scan. The longer support entries each occupy two lines, preserving a consistent rhythm across the last two rows.

general: Allocate width according to content and reading task, rather than distributing it evenly.
Keep row identifiers intact and make numeric columns easy to compare.
Judge wrapping by its effect on hierarchy and row rhythm, not by line count alone.
specific: Support channels need the largest share of width because their descriptions are much longer than the other cells.
About 121px lets the service-credit header fit on one line; the uptime header needs more width to avoid a third line.

final.tradeoffs: Narrower numeric columns give support descriptions more space, but can wrap their headers. r2A offers a little more room for uptime at the expense of support; r1C gives support more room but wraps both numeric headers.
final.uncertain: The ranges are approximate visual judgments based on the supplied renders, not independently tested thresholds. They describe individual column widths with the remaining space redistributed proportionally; combinations at the ends of all ranges may not retain the same wrapping.

A.why: Row labels stay intact and support descriptions have ample space, but the uptime header stacks over three lines, making the header unusually deep.

B.why: The row labels remain intact and the two-line headers are readable, though splitting Service credit adds height to the header.

C.why: Both row labels and Service credit stay on one line, while the uptime header and longer support descriptions wrap cleanly. The columns are well balanced for scanning.

D.why: Wide tier and numeric columns leave support channels cramped; descriptions wrap into many short lines and make rows unnecessarily tall.

E.why: The row labels stay intact and the support descriptions have room to read, though Service credit wraps into two lines.

F.why: The support descriptions and numeric columns scan reasonably well, but Mission-critical breaks across lines in the row-label column.

reviews.unsure: B and E are close alternatives; the preference for C depends partly on valuing the single-line Service credit header.

A.why: The three short-content columns consume most of the width, leaving support descriptions in narrow, fragmented lines and making rows unnecessarily tall.

B.why: Support descriptions have room to read, and tier names stay intact. The uptime header is squeezed into three lines, making the header disproportionately tall.

C.why: Tier names remain intact, and the support descriptions read comfortably in two lines. Both numeric headers wrap, but the columns remain clear.

D.why: The tier names stay intact, and the wide support column gives the longer descriptions a comfortable two-line rhythm. Both numeric headers wrap.

E.why: The support column reads well, but the narrow first column breaks Mission-critical across lines, weakening the row label.

F.why: Tier names and the service credit header stay on one line, while the support descriptions wrap into manageable two-line blocks. The numeric columns are compact and easy to compare.
